title: Crispy Honey-Lime Chicken Rice Bowls
dek: Crisp chicken bites in a tangy honey-lime glaze with peppers, cucumber, and rice.
image_alt: Glazed crispy chicken and vegetables over rice
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions.name: Coat the chicken
instructions.text: Pat chicken dry and toss with cornstarch and salt until lightly coated.

instructions.name: Crisp
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken in one layer until browned and cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes total.

instructions.name: Cook the peppers
instructions.text: Transfer chicken out. Add peppers to the same pan and cook 3 minutes so they stay crisp.

instructions.name: Glaze
instructions.text: Whisk honey, soy sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar, and ginger. Return chicken and toss until the glaze bubbles and clings.

instructions.name: Serve
instructions.text: Spoon over rice with cucumber, sesame seeds, and scallions.

why_it_works: Cornstarch creates crisp edges without deep-frying.
Lime and vinegar keep the honey glaze bright instead of sticky-sweet.
Cucumber adds fresh crunch after the hot glaze.
swaps: Use shrimp and shorten the cook time.
Add steamed broccoli instead of peppers.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet for the best texture.
notes: Give chicken space in the pan or it will steam.
The glaze thickens fast once it boils; toss constantly.

faqs.a: Yes. Spray lightly with oil and bake at 450°F for about 18 minutes, then glaze.

Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

title: Garlic-Scallion Steak Rice Bowls
dek: Seared steak, jammy egg, cucumber, and garlicky soy glaze over rice with enough sauce for every bite.
image_alt: Sliced steak rice bowl with egg cucumber and scallions
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips

instructions.name: Season the steak
instructions.text: Pat steak dry and season with salt and pepper. Let it sit while the skillet heats.

instructions.name: Sear
instructions.text: Heat oil in a cast-iron skillet until shimmering. Sear steak 3 to 5 minutes per side depending on thickness. Rest 8 minutes.

instructions.name: Make the glaze
instructions.text: In the same skillet, add soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, and sesame oil. Simmer 60 seconds.

instructions.name: Slice
instructions.text: Cut steak thinly across the grain and toss lightly with a spoonful of glaze.

instructions.name: Build
instructions.text: Divide rice among bowls and top with steak, egg, cucumber, scallions, nori, and remaining glaze.

why_it_works: High heat gives flank steak deep browning before the center overcooks.
The pan glaze captures the steak fond instead of leaving it behind.
storage: Refrigerate steak and rice up to 4 days. Keep cucumber and egg separate until serving.
notes: Slice across the grain for tenderness.
Flank steak can go from medium to well-done quickly; use an instant-read thermometer if needed.

faqs.a: Yes. Grill over high heat, then make the glaze in a small saucepan.
Absolutely. Day-old rice reheats well for bowls.

faqs.q: How do I make it spicy?
faqs.a: Add gochujang, chili crisp, or sliced jalapeño.

title: Roasted Garlic Chicken & Mushroom Pasta
dek: Grilled chicken, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, and Parmesan in a glossy roasted-garlic cream sauce.
image_alt: Grilled chicken pasta with mushrooms tomatoes and Parmesan

instructions.name: Cook the pasta
instructions.text: Boil pasta until just shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.

instructions.name: Sear the chicken
instructions.text: Season chicken and cook in olive oil 4 to 6 minutes per side until 165°F. Rest, then slice.

instructions.name: Brown the vegetables
instructions.text: Add mushrooms to the skillet and brown well. Add tomatoes for the final 2 minutes.

instructions.name: Make the sauce
instructions.text: Stir in roasted garlic, broth, and cream. Simmer 3 minutes, then add Parmesan.

instructions.name: Toss
instructions.text: Add pasta and enough pasta water to make the sauce glossy. Top with sliced chicken and parsley.

why_it_works: Roasted garlic gives sweetness without harsh raw-garlic bite.
Mushrooms brown in the chicken pan and absorb savory fond.
Pasta water keeps the cream sauce fluid and clingy.
swaps: Use half-and-half for a lighter sauce.
Add spinach during the final toss.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat over low heat with a splash of broth.
notes: Brown mushrooms before salting so they do not release water too early.
Do not boil hard after adding Parmesan.

faqs.q: How do I roast garlic quickly?
faqs.a: Wrap peeled cloves with a drizzle of oil in foil and roast at 400°F for about 25 minutes.

faqs.q: Can I use jarred roasted garlic?
faqs.a: Yes. Drain it well before mashing.

faqs.q: Can I make it without cream?
faqs.a: Use 1 extra cup broth and finish with 2 tablespoons butter.

title: Harissa Lamb Meatballs with Herbed Couscous
dek: Spiced lamb meatballs, lemony couscous, tomato-cucumber salad, and cool feta yogurt.
image_alt: Lamb meatballs with couscous tomatoes and yogurt sauce

instructions.name: Mix the meatballs
instructions.text: Combine lamb, beef, harissa, garlic, cumin, coriander, and salt. Form 16 small meatballs.

instructions.name: Roast
instructions.text: Bake at 450°F for 12 to 15 minutes until browned and 160°F.

instructions.name: Make couscous
instructions.text: Bring broth to a boil, stir in couscous, cover, and remove from heat for 5 minutes. Fluff with lemon zest and half the herbs.

instructions.name: Mix the yogurt
instructions.text: Stir yogurt, feta, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.

instructions.name: Plate
instructions.text: Serve meatballs over couscous with cucumber, tomato, onion, feta yogurt, and remaining herbs.

why_it_works: Small meatballs brown quickly without drying out.
Harissa seasons the meat from the inside instead of acting only as a topping.
Cool yogurt balances lamb richness and chile heat.
swaps: Use all beef or ground turkey.
Swap couscous for rice or quinoa.
Use a mild roasted-red-pepper paste instead of harissa for kids.
storage: Refrigerate meatballs and couscous up to 4 days. Keep salad and yogurt separate.
notes: Do not overwork the meat mixture.
Wet your hands lightly before shaping to prevent sticking.
